headline: Computational methods for small-molecule identification and property prediction
label: Computational Molecular Benchmarking Methods
summary: Open benchmarks, curation pipelines, and closed-loop frameworks are standardizing evaluation of computational methods for molecular prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is benchmarking and standardization of computational methods that infer molecular identity or properties from indirect data. FlexMS provides a modular public-data benchmark for MS/MS spectrum prediction across molecular encoders, metadata conditioning, and retrieval, while ChemTorch offers reproducible benchmarking of chemical reaction property prediction with OOD splitters. A community blind challenge evaluates methods for SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV Mpro potency and ligand poses, and MEHC-Curation automates validation, cleaning, and duplicate removal of SMILES datasets for QSAR. What is new is the closed-loop design of Cycle-MS, which couples inverse spectrum-to-molecule prediction with forward spectrum reconstruction through cycle-consistency losses. SPECTRE extends spectrum-based annotation to NMR data with a collision-free fingerprint. RevelioPlots, focused on AI-predicted protein model quality, shares the emphasis on accessible assessment tooling.
